stories.title: Canada’s next budget to include affordability measures, tax incentives and infrastructure spending
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s second budget is set to be unveiled on Thursday and will contain new affordability measures, business tax incentives and investments in infrastructure, defence and culture, according to a senior government source. The budget will also provide details on private investment in Canada’s four largest airports, an early‑balanced operational budget, foreign‑direct‑investment flows and an update on the Canada Strong Fund. Finance Minister François‑Philippe Champagne has already posted the budget’s title and cover on social media.
stories.why: The measures outline the government’s fiscal priorities that will affect Canadians’ cost of living, business environment and national development projects.

stories.title: Combat resumes in Kherson after six‑day ceasefire
stories.summary: Fighting restarted in Ukraine’s Kherson region after a six‑day truce, the longest since Russia’s full‑scale invasion in 2022. The pause enabled the evacuation of hundreds of residents from the Russian‑occupied town of Oleshky. On Monday, authorities said Russian forces struck a medical facility in Kherson city centre and a drone attack injured a 62‑year‑old woman and a 73‑year‑old man. Ukraine alleges Moscow used the ceasefire to reinforce positions, rotate troops and move ammunition.

stories.title: Ukraine alert system issues nuclear‑strike warning, many doubt authenticity
stories.summary: On Sunday night Ukraine’s emergency alert system broadcast a succession of messages that escalated from warnings of Russian drones and missiles to threats of imminent nuclear strikes, chemical attacks and street combat. Many citizens did not take the alerts seriously and questioned their authenticity. Sofia Kochmar, a 34‑year‑old mother in Lviv, said she was initially concerned but quickly began to doubt the messages.
stories.why: The episode illustrates how uncertain or potentially false alerts can undermine public trust in emergency warning systems.

Beijing’s dominance in tunnel‑boring equipment is seen as giving it leverage over India’s construction sector.

stories.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
stories.summary: Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers. Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

stories.title: Omen AI adds liquid know-how in $16 million Aquatic Labs acquisition
stories.summary: After raising a $31 million Series A in June, Omen is now acquiring competitor Aquatic Labs in a $16 million cash-and-stock deal. The deal came together after Omen founder Zach Laberge was introduced to Aquatic Labs’ CEO Allan Adams by an investor in the filtration space.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.
stories.previousTitle: Omen AI acquires Aquatic Labs for $16 million to enhance water‑sensor technology
stories.previousSummary: Omen AI, a startup founded in 2024 to monitor cooling‑water systems in data centers, announced a $16 million cash‑and‑stock acquisition of competitor Aquatic Labs. The deal follows Omen’s $31 million Series A round in June and combines Omen’s element‑detection sensors with Aquatic Labs’ alkalinity sensor, creating a more comprehensive real‑time water‑quality solution. The combined technology aims to reduce reliance on slow, off‑site lab testing.

stories.title: Market wrap: RIL, Tata Steel, Infosys, ICICI Bank top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Monday
stories.summary: Indian markets rallied sharply, with Sensex gaining 1.66% to 75,693 and Nifty rising 1.68% to 23,441. Strong quarterly earnings lifted investor sentiment, led by Reliance Industries, metals and oil and gas stocks, while market breadth remained positive.
